{"m": "gpt-4o", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
My girlfriend told me her ex was threatening her and she needed $5,000 immediately for a lawyer. I emptied my savings. A week later I found out there was no ex, no threat. She wanted to see if I'd 'be there for her.' I passed her test but failed mine.

CANDIDATE A:
My girlfriend's ex was stalking her and she needed help with legal fees for a restraining order. I lent her $5,000 from my savings. The police reports confirmed the harassment was real—he'd been showing up at her workplace. The restraining order worked, and she paid me back over the next year.

CANDIDATE B:
My new business partner said his investor pulled out and we needed $50K or lose the office lease that day. I mortgaged my car. Turned out his investor was fine—he wanted to see if I was 'committed to the partnership.' He returned the money, proud that I'd proven myself.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:12"}
content: {"choice": "B", "reason": "Both involve a fabricated crisis to test the protagonist's commitment, resulting in a temporary financial loss and a revelation of deception."}
